liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Estimated Prophet** (2 reviews): Reviewer calls the Estimated into Eyes pairing a ripping highlight and an all-time favorite; Second set hits stride with an awesome Estimated into Eyes pairing [28][38]
- **Goodnight Irene** (2 reviews): Phil tried starting Morning Dew, but Jerry insisted on Goodnight Irene with Rick Danko; Goodnight Irene has a cool arrangement, unlike the otherwise typical setlist for the period [27][32]
- **Peggy-O** (1 review): Reviewer found the first-set Peggy-O incredible [27]
- **Eyes Of The World** (1 review): After Jerry rises following the second verse of Eyes, band, crowd and Jerry reach incredible levels [33]
- **Brokedown Palace** (1 review): Reviewer singles out Brokedown Palace and Midnight Hour as favorites [32]

## Setlist highlights

- **Bill G as Big Brother**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [39]
- **Interviews**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [39]
- **NYE Countdown (Tsaichovsky's 1812 Overture)**: back after 736 archived shows (4017 days); rare: 6 archived performances [39]
- **Big Boss Man**: back after 133 archived shows (730 days) [39]
- **Goodnight Irene**: earliest performance in the archive; mythic rare: 2 archived performances [39]

## The recordings

- **gd1983-12-31.155215.5-1.tobin.flac1648** (recommended): source not stated; 24 songs; 183 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [1]
- **gd83-12-31.sbd.bertha-ashley.14948.sbeok.shnf**: pre-FM broadcast master; 23 songs; 161 min; rated 4.25/5 by 8 [2]. Said about its sound: Listener hears constant clicking from the left speaker in the first three shortened files; Replier says the clicking is the well-defined bass drum, especially early in the recording [34][37]
- **gd1983-12-31.164337.senn441.vita..miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 23 songs; 166 min [3]
- **gd1983-12-31.148208.fob.akg.d330bt.senn421.hecht.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 23 songs; 157 min [5]
- **gd83-12-31.sbd.miller.13963.sbeok.shnf**: pre-FM broadcast master; 22 songs; 161 min; rated 3.43/5 by 14 [15]. Said about its sound: Brief dropout about 23 seconds into Touch of Grey; easily repaired; Right channel level drops severely around 8:25 in Eyes of the World; fixable with Sound Forge; Reviewer describes Brother Esau and Throwing Stones as crisp on this tape [30][31][32]
- **gd83-12-31.beyer.walstib.18737.sbeok.shnf**: source not stated; 21 songs; 157 min; rated 4.5/5 by 4 [20]. Said about its sound: Beyer audience recording has outstanding fidelity, clearer than the soundboard on songs like Jack Straw [38]

## Around the show

- The encore came after the second set, which the reviewer attributes to Bill Graham rushing the stage to prevent a third set [27]
- Reviewer attended; first New Year's Eve back in San Francisco since Winterland's closing [28]
- The Band opened the show, among their first gigs after reforming without Robbie Robertson; Maria Muldaur sang on the encores [29]
- Members of The Band joined in the first set, playing Mystery Train and other songs [31]
- Midnight Hour lineup: Mickey Hart on drums and cowbell, Rick Danko acoustic guitar and vocals, Maria Muldaur vocals and tambourine, Terry Cagle tambourine and drums [1]
- Set III Midnight Hour featured Mickey Hart, Rick Danko, Maria Muldaur and Terry Cagle on percussion and vocals [3]
- Midnight Hour guests: Rick Danko, Maria Muldaur, Terry Cagle, with Mickey Hart on cowbell [5]
- Reviewer felt the Dead seemed flat and a bit nervous next to The Band's set [29]
- Reviewer ranks its fidelity alongside digital recordings starting with Compton Terrace in early 1983 [38]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1983-12-31.155215.5-1.tobin.flac1648**: transferred by 5.1 LPCM Surround Sound Mix (48k) by Kevin Tobin; source: 5.1 LPCM Surround Sound (48k) mixed in Adobe Audition CC 2014 [1]. Also: Mixed by an archive.org user; FLAC conversion dated 10 January 2022 by Trader Little Helper [1]
- **gd83-12-31.sbd.bertha-ashley.14948.sbeok.shnf**: source: Pre-FM>Cm>Cass>Dat>CD - Sound C- [2]. Also: Source chain: pre-FM broadcast, to cassette master, to cassette, to DAT, to CD; sound rated C minus [2]
- **gd1983-12-31.164337.senn441.vita..miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Jim Vita; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Jim Vita's Master Audience Cassettes; Sennheiser 441 mics > Sony D5M (Maxell UDXLII-S) [3]. Also: A Nakamichi 700 source supplies a 9-second patch in Space [3]
- **gd1983-12-31.148208.fob.akg.d330bt.senn421.hecht.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Chris Hecht; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Chris Hecht's Master Audience Cassettes; (2) AKG D330BT mics + (1) Sennheiser 421 > Fostex Mixer > Sony D5M [5]. Also: A matrix source patches 5 seconds of Tennessee Jed's start and 5:15 of Drums into Space [5]
- **gd83-12-31.sbd.miller.13963.sbeok.shnf**: source: SBD -> Rm -> Dat -> M-Audio 2448 -> Samplitude 2496 v6.0 -> CD (SHN)Brokedown Palace patched from Pre-FM>Cm>Cass>Dat>CDDat -> SHN Transfer Done By Charlie an… [15]
- **gd83-12-31.beyer.walstib.18737.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Walstib; source: 3 Beyer M160 FOB> Sony TCD5M Master Cassette>shn [20]

claims.text: Reviewer found the first-set Peggy-O incredible
Phil tried starting Morning Dew, but Jerry insisted on Goodnight Irene with Rick Danko
The encore came after the second set, which the reviewer attributes to Bill Graham rushing the stage to prevent a third set
Reviewer calls the Estimated into Eyes pairing a ripping highlight and an all-time favorite
Reviewer attended; first New Year's Eve back in San Francisco since Winterland's closing
The Band opened the show, among their first gigs after reforming without Robbie Robertson; Maria Muldaur sang on the encores
Reviewer felt the Dead seemed flat and a bit nervous next to The Band's set
Brief dropout about 23 seconds into Touch of Grey; easily repaired
Right channel level drops severely around 8:25 in Eyes of the World; fixable with Sound Forge
Members of The Band joined in the first set, playing Mystery Train and other songs
Reviewer describes Brother Esau and Throwing Stones as crisp on this tape
Sound is very good but with a lot of hiss
Goodnight Irene has a cool arrangement, unlike the otherwise typical setlist for the period
Reviewer singles out Brokedown Palace and Midnight Hour as favorites
After Jerry rises following the second verse of Eyes, band, crowd and Jerry reach incredible levels
Listener hears constant clicking from the left speaker in the first three shortened files
Replier says the clicking is the well-defined bass drum, especially early in the recording
Beyer audience recording has outstanding fidelity, clearer than the soundboard on songs like Jack Straw
Reviewer ranks its fidelity alongside digital recordings starting with Compton Terrace in early 1983
Second set hits stride with an awesome Estimated into Eyes pairing
Midnight Hour lineup: Mickey Hart on drums and cowbell, Rick Danko acoustic guitar and vocals, Maria Muldaur vocals and tambourine, Terry Cagle tambourine and drums
Mixed by an archive.org user; FLAC conversion dated 10 January 2022 by Trader Little Helper
Source chain: pre-FM broadcast, to cassette master, to cassette, to DAT, to CD; sound rated C minus
Master cassettes came from Jim Vita; Charlie Miller transferred and coordinated; Sennheiser 421 source supplies all of Brokedown Palace
A Nakamichi 700 source supplies a 9-second patch in Space
Set III Midnight Hour featured Mickey Hart, Rick Danko, Maria Muldaur and Terry Cagle on percussion and vocals
Master recording from Chris Hecht; transfer by Charlie Miller, using AKG, Sennheiser 421 and other mics
A matrix source patches 5 seconds of Tennessee Jed's start and 5:15 of Drums into Space
Midnight Hour guests: Rick Danko, Maria Muldaur, Terry Cagle, with Mickey Hart on cowbell
